info.title: Cylist
info.description:
Cylist keeps a project's **board**, **files**, **vault** and **people** in one
place — for you in the browser, and for your agents over the same HTTP API.

Authenticate with either an `Authorization: Bearer cyl_…` header or the
session cookie set by `POST /auth/login`. Tokens carry scopes; read each
endpoint's description to see which one it needs.

get.description:
Report whether the API can serve requests.

Returns ``503`` when the database is unreachable so orchestrators stop
routing traffic here.

Responses served since this process started, by status class.

Unauthenticated, like ``/health``: it reveals traffic volume and nothing
about its content. Counts reset on every restart — read alongside
``since``, not as a running total across deploys.

How many sockets this process is holding.

The answer to a question that is otherwise unanswerable after the fact:
did the WebSocket upgrade actually survive the proxy in production, on a
day nobody was watching? A board that has silently fallen back to polling
looks exactly like a working one from the outside, and shows up here as
watchers that never arrive.

Unauthenticated for the reason the other two are, and safe to be: counts
only. No project, no session, no token, nothing about content.
Describe this deployment to a client that is configuring itself.

post.description:
Exchange an email and password for a session cookie.

Omitting the email asks for the bootstrap login, which is refused unless
the directory holds nobody who can sign in. See the module note.

The session the browser already held, if any, is revoked; and if this
person now holds more than ten live sessions, the oldest are revoked too.

429.description: Too many attempts; `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

post.summary: Set a password from an invitation
post.description:
Turn an invitation link into an account, and sign in with it.

Unauthenticated by necessity: the whole point is that whoever holds the
link has no credential yet. The link *is* the credential, which is why it
is one-time, expiring, and stored only as a digest — and why a link
accepted twice at the same moment opens exactly one account.

422.description: The invitation is unknown, spent or expired.

429.description: Too many attempts; `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

post.description:
Replace your own password, proving you know the current one.

Every other credential you hold is revoked — that is the point of changing
a password under suspicion — and this session is re-issued, so the browser
you did it in stays signed in and every other one does not.

Revoke the current session and clear its cookie.

Safe to call without a session; it simply clears the cookie.

get.description:
Return who the caller is and which scopes they hold.

Useful to a CLI or MCP server for checking a token before it starts work,
and to the web app, which asks once and then knows which person in every
list it is looking at is itself.

Every live browser session of the person this credential acts as,
newest first, with when each was last used and which one this is.

Only sessions. API tokens are listed under ``GET /tokens``.

Yours alone: somebody else's session, or a session already ended, is a

exist. Ending the session making the request is allowed — it is a logout.

post.description:
Mint a token and return its plaintext exactly once.

Grant the narrowest useful set of scopes: an agent that only rearranges the
board needs ``read`` and ``write``, never ``vault:reveal``.

The token acts as whoever minted it. An agent moving a card writes that
person's name into the card's history, which is the answer everybody
wants to "who moved this?" — "an API token" never was, and with several
people on one board it would be an answer that names nobody.

Its scopes must be ones the caller holds, and `permit` can only be
granted from a browser session.

403.description: A scope asked for is one the caller does not hold.

delete.description:
Revoke a token immediately. Requests using it stop working at once.

Needs ``admin``, except to revoke the very token making the request: any
credential may sign itself out (the phone app does, with its own id from
``GET /me``).

Idempotent: send it after every sign-in and whenever Firebase rotates the
token. A token another person registered moves to the caller, since an
install is used by whoever is signed in on it now.

The device is sent to while the credential that registered it stays live;
revoking that token stops its pushes.

delete.description:
Delete a project, and with it everything filed under it.

Its board and every card on it, the folders and the uploaded bytes nothing
else is holding, the docs, the vault and its secrets, the roles and who
wore them. None of it comes back. Only the audit log survives, with the
record of what happened on a project that is no longer there.

Archiving is the reversible answer and is a different call: `PATCH` with
`{"archived": true}` takes a project off the grid and leaves all of the
above where it is.

`confirm` has to be the project's own key. It is not ceremony — this path
archived a project until CYLIST-73, so a caller written against the old
meaning has to say something new before the new one runs, and gets a 422
rather than a destroyed board.

Set the project's membership to exactly these people.

This replaces the list rather than adding to it: anyone not named is
removed from the project. They stay in the directory, and anything they are
already assigned keeps naming them.

permission is the baseline's, so every member holds it; without this
fence a member could drop the admin, inherit the vacancy and add them back
with no role. For the same reason the vacancy is only filled on an admin's
save — handing out the role is never a side effect of somebody else's.

get.description:
What happened on this project on one day, grouped by card.

Everything here is already in `/activity`; this is that trail cut at the
boundaries of one local day and turned into an account of the work — each
card that was touched, what happened to it in order, and which cards
ended the day in the board's last column.

A day means midnight to midnight in `timezone`, not in UTC, because the day
being asked about is the one the asker just lived. The window it settled on
comes back as `starts_at` and `ends_at` so there is no doubt about what was
covered.

`todos` is the caller's own plan for the day — the cards they picked up on
Today and their to-dos under each, with what became of each one. Nobody
else's plan is included.

`markdown` is the whole report as a paste-ready note. It is written here
rather than by each client so a stand-up note copied out of the browser and
one written by an agent say the same thing.

A card's moves are reported as the one move they amounted to: a card
dragged To do → In progress → Dev in a day got from To do to Dev, and the
columns in between are where it was passing through. `moves` in that
entry's payload says how many drags it stands for, and the card's own
`/history` still holds every one of them.

Changes that altered nothing — a card dragged within its own column, a form
saved without an edit — are left out, exactly as they are in a card's
history. `/activity` remains the place that answers "who touched what".

patch.summary: Tick, untick or reword a to-do
patch.description:
Tick, untick or reword a to-do.

A to-do that came from the card ticks the card too: a sub-task is
finished or reopened, a tick box ticked or reopened, and a stage moves the
card on to the stage after it (or back to it, when unticked). Each is
checked against the caller's role and written to the card's history
exactly as doing it on the board would be. Giving up on one (`not_done`)
is the plan's business alone and leaves the card as it is, and so is
reopening one that was given up on: only unticking a done one unticks the
card.

post.description:
Close a day: move the chosen open to-dos on to `to_day`, leave the rest as not done.

A moved to-do stays on its day as `moved`, and a copy starts open on
`to_day` under the same card — which is put on that day if it was not
there already. To-dos already done are left alone.

get.description:
Every node in the tree the caller is cleared for, nested, with each
secret's metadata.

No secret value appears here at any depth. Call
`POST /vault/nodes/{id}/reveal` for one of those, one at a time.

The counts are of what came back rather than of what is there, so the
header over a filtered tree agrees with the rows under it.

post.summary: Add a branch or a secret
post.description:
Create a node.

A `branch` groups other nodes. A `secret` carries one credential, given as
`secret.value`; it is encrypted before it is stored and the response does
not contain it.

409.description: A sibling already has that name.

patch.summary: Rename a node, or amend its secret
patch.description:
Change any subset of a node. Omitted fields are left alone.

Supplying `secret.value` re-encrypts under a fresh nonce; omitting it
leaves the stored credential untouched, so a username or a note can be
corrected without knowing it.

409.description: A sibling already has that name.

delete.description: Delete a node. A branch takes its whole subtree with it.

post.description:
Re-parent and reposition a node within its tree.

`parent_id` is always the destination: `null` means the top level, not
"leave it where it is". Moving a branch into its own subtree is refused —
it would detach that subtree from the tree entirely.

409.description: Something of that name is already there.

422.description: The destination is inside the node being moved.

post.description:
Decrypt one credential and return it.

The only endpoint in Cylist that does. `POST` rather than `GET` on purpose:
revealing a credential is an event with a consequence, it must not be
cached by a proxy, and it must not sit in a browser's history or a server
access log as a URL anyone can replay.

Every call is written to the activity feed naming the node, so the log
answers "who looked at the Twilio password, and when?". The plaintext
itself is never recorded.

403.description: This token does not hold `vault:reveal`.

422.description: That node is a branch, so it holds no credential.

that should come with it.

Cylist sends no email, so the link comes back here for you to pass on. It
is shown once; ask again and the old one stops working.

post.summary: Upload a skill, as one file or as a folder
post.description:
Upload a skill as `multipart/form-data`.

**A skill can be a whole folder.** A skill is usually a `SKILL.md` beside
the scripts and references it points an agent at, so send one `file` part
per file, each named with its path inside the folder, and `folder` with
the folder's own name. The server lays it out, checks it the way it checks
an uploaded zip — a root `SKILL.md`, nothing pointing outside the folder,
at most 200 files and 20 MB — and stores it as `<folder>.zip`, which
`/skills/{skill_id}/folder` unpacks again file for file. A single part with
no `folder` is stored exactly as it was sent, as it always was.

**Uploading a name that already exists replaces it** and answers 200 rather
than 201 — the name is the skill, so sending `board-tidy.md` again means
you have a newer version of it, not that you have a conflict. This is the
one place Cylist's upload rules differ from the file tree's, where a
duplicate name is refused.

Content is addressed by its SHA-256 and shared with the file store, so
uploading bytes the server already holds costs a row and no disk.

**It is filed under whoever is uploading it** — the person behind the
session or token — and there is no field to say otherwise (CYLIST-142).
An agent's upload is its owner's, which is the person its token acts as.

description.description: What belongs in this column. Required — an unexplained column drifts.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
outcomes.description: The ways work can end in this column — 'Done', 'Cancelled', 'In prod' — as sections the column is divided into, left to right. Only the board's last column may have any; anywhere else this must be empty. Leave it empty to draw no distinction.

column_id.title: Column Id
column_id.description: One of the project's columns, and not the last one: a card is done when it reaches the end of the board, so the date for the last column is the card's own `due_date`.

ColumnDueDateInput.title: ColumnDueDateInput
ColumnDueDateInput.description: A date this card is wanted in one column by.

column_id.title: Column Id
column_id.description: One of the project's columns, and not the last one: a card is done when it reaches the end of the board, so the date for the last column is the card's own `due_date`.

column_name.title: Column Name
column_name.description: That column's name, so a card reads alone.

met.title: Met
met.description: Whether the card has reached that column. A met date is behind the card and stops being asked anything of — it never reads as late, and `next_due_date` skips it.

ColumnDueDateRead.title: ColumnDueDateRead
ColumnDueDateRead.description: One of those dates, with what a reader needs to make sense of it.

column_ids.title: Column Ids
column_ids.description: Every column on the board, in the order you want them. Naming a subset is an error rather than a partial reorder.

ColumnOrder.title: ColumnOrder
ColumnOrder.description: Reorders a board left to right.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
outcomes.description: The sections this column is divided into, left to right. Empty on every column but the board's last, and on a last column that draws no distinction. A card in this column names its own by `outcome_index`.

task_count.title: Task Count
task_count.description: How many cards are currently in this column.

name.title: Name
name.description: The column's name, so a grid needs no second call.

may_enter.title: May Enter
may_enter.description: Whether a card may be moved into it.

may_stage.title: May Stage
may_stage.description: Whether the sub-stages a card passes through here may be set — both the template's rule for this column and a card's own bar.

ColumnRule.title: ColumnRule
ColumnRule.description: What one role may do at one column of the board.

ColumnRuleInput.title: ColumnRuleInput
ColumnRuleInput.description: One column of a role's workflow line.

ColumnRulesUpdate.title: ColumnRulesUpdate
ColumnRulesUpdate.description:
Replaces a role's whole line across the board.

The whole board every time, for the reason a permission row is replaced
whole: the screen has the line in front of it, and a delta is how two
admins on two tabs end up with the union of what each of them meant.
Columns left out of the list are left unrestricted.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
outcomes.description: Replaces the column's sections outright. Shortening the list moves any card past its end into the last section still standing; emptying it takes every card in the column out of a section altogether.

ColumnUpdate.title: ColumnUpdate
ColumnUpdate.description: Every field optional; omitted fields are left as they are.

author_id.title: Author Id
author_id.description: Who is speaking. Must be a project member. Omit for an agent.

CommentKind.title: CommentKind
CommentKind.description: Who wrote a timeline entry, in effect.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: For a `status_change`: `{from, to, reason, tagged}`. Empty otherwise.

day.title: Day
day.description: The day this reports on, in `timezone`.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: The IANA zone the day was cut by, e.g. `Asia/Kolkata`. The zone the request settled on, which for a loosely spelled one is not the name it asked with — this is the one to trust.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: Midnight that began the day, in UTC.

ends_at.title: Ends At
ends_at.description: Midnight that ended it, in UTC. Exclusive: an entry at exactly this moment belongs to the next day.

entry_count.title: Entry Count
entry_count.description: How many lines the report holds — a card's day of moves counting as the one move it amounted to, not as each drag.

finished.title: Finished
finished.description: References of the cards that ended the day in the board's last column.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.description: The cards touched today, in the order they were first touched.

elsewhere.title: Elsewhere
elsewhere.description: Changes that were not to a card — files, columns, the vault, the project itself — oldest first.

todos.title: Todos
todos.description: The asker's own plan for the day — the cards they picked up and their to-dos under each — in the order picked. Empty for anyone who did not plan the day, and always for the bootstrap session, which is nobody.

markdown.title: Markdown
markdown.description: The whole report as Markdown, worded by the server so a stand-up note pasted from the browser and one written by an agent read the same.

DayReport.title: DayReport
DayReport.description:
What one project's day amounted to, ready to be read or pasted.

Grouped by card rather than left as a flat feed, because a day spent on
four cards is four pieces of work and thirty audit rows — the grouping is
the part that turns the record into a report. Condensed for the same
reason: a card's moves collapse to where it started and where it ended, so
a card walked across the board reads as one step rather than four.

state.description: `done`, `moved` (to `moved_to`), `not_done`, or `open` for a day that has not been wrapped up yet.

carried_from.title: Carried From
carried_from.description: The day it was moved on from, if it was.

DayTodo.title: DayTodo
DayTodo.description: One to-do from the asker's plan for the day, and how the day left it.

DeliveryState.title: DeliveryState
DeliveryState.description: Where an event is on its way to a hook's URL.

DevicePlatform.title: DevicePlatform
DevicePlatform.description: Which push service a device's token belongs to.

token_id.title: Token Id
token_id.description: The API token the device registered with.

DeviceRead.title: DeviceRead
DeviceRead.description: A registered device. Its FCM token is never sent back.

fcm_token.title: Fcm Token
fcm_token.description: The registration token Firebase Cloud Messaging gave this app install. Registering one that is already known moves it to the caller.

label.title: Label
label.description: What the device is called, as a person would recognise it.

status.title: Status
status.description: `ok`: `found` answers it — work from it. `ambiguous`: `found` passed the check but the route was close; glance at `alternatives`. `unverified`: no section passed the check, and `found` is only the best guess. `not_documented`: nothing written on it. `unavailable`: jev could not be asked — `reason` says why. Anything but `ok` and `ambiguous` means: find it in the code, then `place` it.

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description: The relevance an answer must reach to be `ok`.

also.description: When the question asks both why and how: the other side's section.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why jev was not asked, or what it noted.

DocAnswer.title: DocAnswer
DocAnswer.description: Where the docs answer a question, and how sure jev is that they do.

DocListing.title: DocListing
DocListing.description: A doc as the tree draws it: everything but the body.

doc_ids.title: Doc Ids
doc_ids.description: Every doc in the topic, exactly once, top first.

DocOrder.title: DocOrder
DocOrder.description: Every doc in one topic, in the order they should be drawn.

title.title: Title
title.description: A short name for what you found.

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: The names a reader would type to find it: `move_task`, `Book C`.

DocPlace.title: DocPlace
DocPlace.description: What an agent found in the code, to be told where in the docs it goes.

question.title: Question
question.description: What you would otherwise open the code to find out, as you would ask a colleague: "where is the check that stops a sub-task being moved?"

DocRead.title: DocRead
DocRead.description: One doc, its markdown included, and where it is filed.

DocSection.title: DocSection
DocSection.description: One of the two headings every project's docs are filed under.

topic_ids.title: Topic Ids
topic_ids.description: Every topic in the section, exactly once, top first.

DocTopicOrder.title: DocTopicOrder
DocTopicOrder.description: Every topic in one section, in the order they should be drawn.

DocTopicUpdate.title: DocTopicUpdate
DocTopicUpdate.description:
Rename a topic. A topic does not change section: its docs were filed as
product or engineering, and moving the heading would refile all of them.

DocTree.title: DocTree
DocTree.description:
A project's docs, as the Docs page draws them.

Both sections, always, in the same order — an empty section is still a
heading somebody can add a topic under. Bodies are left out: the tree is
for finding a doc, and `GET /docs/{id}` is for reading one.

topic_id.title: Topic Id
topic_id.description: Move the doc to this topic.

position.title: Position
position.description: Where in its topic, counting from the top. Clamped to the topic's length.

DocUpdate.title: DocUpdate
DocUpdate.description:
Every field optional; omitted fields are left as they are.

Moving a doc is setting ``topic_id`` — to another topic on the same
project, in either section. It lands at ``position`` in its new topic, or
at the bottom when that is left out.

topic_id.title: Topic Id
topic_id.description: The topic to file it under — the one `place` named. Leave it out only when the project has a single topic; otherwise the write is refused with the topics to choose from.

append.title: Append
append.description: When the topic already holds a doc of this title, add `body` to the end of it rather than refusing. How a line goes onto a topic's `learned.md`.

DocWrite.title: DocWrite
DocWrite.description: Write a doc onto a project, naming its topic or leaving it to be filed.

created.title: Created
created.description: False when `append` added to a doc already there.

filed_by.title: Filed By
filed_by.description: Who chose the topic: the writer, or nobody because the project has only one.

text.title: Text
text.description: One thing you found, as a sentence the next reader could act on.

shape.title: Shape
shape.description: What kind of fact it is; it steers which section it lands in.

field.title: Field
field.description: The field's name on the record, e.g. `due_date`.

label.title: Label
label.description: How to word it, e.g. `due date`.

from.title: From
from.description: What it said before, rendered the way the card renders it — an assignee by name, a date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Null if it was not set.

FieldChange.title: FieldChange
FieldChange.description: One field of a record, before and after somebody touched it.

sensitivity.description: How far this may travel. A role not cleared this high is not shown it.

folder_path.title: Folder Path
folder_path.description: The folders between the project's root and this item, outermost first, joined by `/`. Empty for an item at the top of the project.

FiledItem.title: FiledItem
FiledItem.description:
A row of the project-wide listing: an item, and where it is filed.

The path is for telling two files of the same name apart. It is a string
rather than a list of crumbs because nothing navigates with it — a picker
shows it beside the name, and the name is what a tag carries.

path.title: Path
path.description: The folders above this one, outermost first, ending with it. Always starts at the project's root.

FolderChildren.title: FolderChildren
FolderChildren.description: What one folder holds — the right-hand pane of the files screen.

parent_id.title: Parent Id
parent_id.description: Omit to put the folder in the project's root folder.

default_sensitivity.description: What things put in this folder are classified as unless the caller says. Omit on create to inherit the parent folder's.

FolderNode.title: FolderNode
FolderNode.description: One folder in the whole-tree response, with its subfolders inside it.

parent_id.title: Parent Id
parent_id.description: Null only for the project's root folder.

is_root.title: Is Root
is_root.description: Whether this is the project's root folder, which is named after the project and cannot be renamed, moved or deleted.

default_sensitivity.description: What things uploaded here are classified as unless the caller says.

FolderUpdate.title: FolderUpdate
FolderUpdate.description:
Rename a folder, move it, or both.

``parent_id`` distinguishes omitted from null: leaving it out keeps the
folder where it is, sending `null` moves it to the project's root.

The root itself accepts neither — it stands for the project, and the API
says so with a 422 rather than silently ignoring the request.

description.title: Description
description.description: What reaching this goal means. Optional, unlike a card's — a goal is a heading its cards spell out underneath.

colour.title: Colour
colour.description: Six-digit hex, drawn as the rail down every card linked to this goal. Omit to take a stable colour from the palette.

target_date.title: Target Date
target_date.description: When the goal is wanted by. Omit it for a goal with no date.

owner_id.title: Owner Id
owner_id.description: Must be a member of the project.

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: `ATL-G1`. Usable in place of the id.

colour.title: Colour
colour.description: Six-digit hex, drawn as the rail on this goal's cards.

target_date.title: Target Date
target_date.description: Null when the goal has no date.

achieved_at.title: Achieved At
achieved_at.description: When it was reached. Null until it is.

GoalDetail.title: GoalDetail
GoalDetail.description:
One goal and the cards linked to it.

The cards come back in board order — left to right by column, top to
bottom within one — so a goal's page can be read as the slice of the board
that belongs to it.

total.title: Total
total.description: Cards linked to this goal, cancelled ones included.

done.title: Done
done.description: Cards in the board's last column. What 'done' means for a card is where it is, so it is where this is counted from.

cancelled.title: Cancelled
cancelled.description: Cards dropped. Settled, but not achieved.

open.title: Open
open.description: Cards that are neither done nor cancelled — what is left. While this is above zero the goal cannot be marked achieved.

GoalProgress.title: GoalProgress
GoalProgress.description:
How far along a goal is, counted from the cards linked to it.

Derived rather than stored: a goal's progress is a reading of its cards,
and a percentage kept in a column beside them is a number that can be
wrong. Cards only — a sub-task belongs to its card, and its card is what
the goal counts.

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: `ATL-G1`. Usable in place of the id.

colour.title: Colour
colour.description: Six-digit hex, drawn as the rail on this goal's cards.

target_date.title: Target Date
target_date.description: Null when the goal has no date.

achieved_at.title: Achieved At
achieved_at.description: When it was reached. Null until it is.

GoalStatus.title: GoalStatus
GoalStatus.description: Whether a goal is still being worked towards, and if not, how it ended.

target_date.title: Target Date
target_date.description: A new date, or null to take the date off the goal. Unlike the other fields here, null means clear rather than leave alone.

status.description: `achieved` is refused while a linked card is still open — the error names what is outstanding. `dropped` is not: giving up on a goal is exactly the thing you do while work on it is unfinished.

GoalUpdate.title: GoalUpdate
GoalUpdate.description:
Every field optional; omitted fields are left as they are.

``status`` is here rather than on a path of its own, unlike a task's: a
task's status change has to carry a reason and be written to a timeline,
while a goal's is one word with nothing owed alongside it. The rule it
does carry — that a goal cannot be achieved over open cards — is enforced
wherever it is set.

actor_label.title: Actor Label
actor_label.description: Who did it — a token's name, or `Web session` for the browser.

channel.description: `web` if a person did it, `api` if an agent did.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: The same thing as one readable sentence.

changes.title: Changes
changes.description: Field-by-field detail, where the event has any. Empty otherwise.

HistoryEntry.title: HistoryEntry
HistoryEntry.description:
One audit entry, worded: what happened, when, and who did it.

The readable half of :class:`ActivityRead`. ``summary`` is written by the
server — see :func:`app.services.activity.describe` — so a card's history,
a day's report, the CLI and an agent all tell the same story in the same
words rather than each keeping a verb-to-sentence map of its own.

url.title: Url
url.description: Where events are POSTed. http:// or https://.

manual.title: Manual
manual.description: Fired by hand, from `POST .../fire`, and never by a change. A manual hook takes no `verbs` and no filters.

verbs.title: Verbs
verbs.description: The events to fire on, from `GET /hooks/events`. Empty fires on all of them.

to_column_id.title: To Column Id
to_column_id.description: Only cards in this column after the change. On `task.moved`, only a move into it from another column.

from_column_id.title: From Column Id
from_column_id.description: Only `task.moved`, and only out of this column.

agent_only.description: Only cards assigned to the agent after the change.

mentions_only.title: Mentions Only
mentions_only.description: Only `task.commented`, and only a comment that tags somebody with `@`.

mentioned_person_id.title: Mentioned Person Id
mentioned_person_id.description: Only `task.commented`, and only a comment that tags this project member.

secret.description: The signing secret to use. Omit to have one generated.

manual.description: Fired by hand only; never by a change.

mentions_only.description: Only comments that tag somebody match.

mentioned_person_name.description: The tagged person's name now, or null if they have been deleted — in which case the filter matches nothing.

secret_hint.title: Secret Hint
secret_hint.description: The signing secret's last four characters.

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: The signing secret. Shown here and when rotated, never again.

label.description: How the Hooks page words it.

hint.title: Hint
hint.description: One line on when it happens. Empty if the label says it.

category.title: Category
category.description: Which group it is offered in, e.g. `moves`.

message.title: Message
message.description: Anything the receiver should be told — sent as `detail.message`.

manual.description: Fired by hand only; never by a change.

to_column_name.description: The column's name now, or null if it has been deleted — in which case the filter matches nothing.

agent_only.title: Agent Only
agent_only.description: Only cards assigned to the agent match.

mentions_only.title: Mentions Only
mentions_only.description: Only comments that tag somebody match.

mentioned_person_name.description: The tagged person's name now, or null if they have been deleted — in which case the filter matches nothing.

secret_hint.description: The signing secret's last four characters.

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: The new signing secret. Omit to have one generated.

manual.title: Manual
manual.description: Make it manual, or put it back on changes. Clear its events and filters in the same request to make it manual.

agent_only.title: Agent Only
agent_only.description: Only cards assigned to the agent. `null` turns it off.

mentions_only.title: Mentions Only
mentions_only.description: Only comments that tag somebody. `null` turns it off.

HookUpdate.title: HookUpdate
HookUpdate.description:
Every field optional. A filter sent as `null` is cleared; one left out is
left alone.

person.description: Who this credential acts as: whoever signed in, or whoever minted the token an agent is using. Null only for the bootstrap session on a deployment with no accounts in it yet, whose first job is to create one.

Identity.title: Identity
Identity.description: Who the current credential belongs to and what it may do.

token.title: Token
token.description: The invitation token from the link.

password.title: Password
password.description: The password they will sign in with from now on.

token.title: Token
token.description: The one-time invitation token. Store nothing; send it once.

url.title: Url
url.description: The full link to give them, built from the request's origin.

InviteIssued.title: InviteIssued
InviteIssued.description:
A freshly minted invitation. The token is shown once and never again.

Cylist does not send email, so the link is handed back to whoever asked
for it to pass on. That is a deliberate stopping point rather than an
omission: a secret that travels by a channel the sender chose is a secret
somebody watched leave.

ItemKind.title: ItemKind
ItemKind.description: Whether an item's content is here or somewhere else.

sensitivity.description: How far this may travel. A role not cleared this high is not shown it.

ItemRead.title: ItemRead
ItemRead.description:
A row of a folder listing.

``added_by`` is the person rather than their id: every listing draws their
avatar and name, so returning an id would make a second request per row
inevitable. The endpoints that *set* it take an id.

ItemSource.title: ItemSource
ItemSource.description: Where an item came from — the listing's Source column.

sensitivity.description: Reclassify it. Needs the `files` permission like any edit.

ItemUpdate.title: ItemUpdate
ItemUpdate.description: Every field optional; omitted fields are left as they are.

sensitivity.description: How far this may travel. Omit to take the folder's default, which is how a folder of contracts stays restricted without anybody remembering to say so on each upload.

LinkCreate.title: LinkCreate
LinkCreate.description: A document that lives in SharePoint, Drive or anywhere else.

email.title: Email
email.description: Omit only while the deployment has no accounts yet.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest
LoginRequest.description:
An email and a password — or, before anybody has an account, just the
password.

``email`` is optional for exactly one case: the first sign-in to a
deployment that has no accounts in it, which is checked against
``CYLIST_PASSWORD_HASH`` and belongs to nobody. ``GET /setup`` says
whether that is where this server is, so the sign-in screen knows which
of the two forms to draw.

is_agent.title: Is Agent
is_agent.description: Whether this entry is the machine rather than a person. It is assigned work like anybody else and never signs in.

has_account.title: Has Account
has_account.description: Whether they can sign in as themselves right now.

invite_is_pending.title: Invite Is Pending
invite_is_pending.description: Whether an unaccepted, unexpired invitation is outstanding.

role.description: Their role on this project, or null if they have none yet.

MemberRead.title: MemberRead
MemberRead.description:
A person as they appear *on a project*, rather than in the directory.

Everything a directory entry has, plus the one thing that only exists once
somebody is on a board: what they are on it. ``role`` is that role and not
the job title, which is :attr:`PersonRead.title` — the two were the same
word until CYLIST-45 and are deliberately no longer.

role.title: Role
role.description: The role's id, or its name (case-insensitive). Null takes their role off and leaves them a member with none.

MemberRoleUpdate.title: MemberRoleUpdate
MemberRoleUpdate.description: Puts one of the project's roles on a member, or takes it off.

person_ids.title: Person Ids
person_ids.description: The complete member list. People not named here are removed.

MembershipUpdate.title: MembershipUpdate
MembershipUpdate.description: Replaces a project's membership with exactly these people.

Permission.title: Permission
Permission.description: One thing a role may allow. The values are stored, so they are stable.

label.title: Label
label.description: The column heading — a couple of words.

PermissionInfoRead.title: PermissionInfoRead
PermissionInfoRead.description: One permission, described well enough to draw a labelled tick box.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.description: Exactly what this role may do afterwards. An empty list allows nothing.

PermissionsUpdate.title: PermissionsUpdate
PermissionsUpdate.description:
Replaces what one role allows.

The whole set every time rather than a delta: the screen has the whole row
in front of it, and a delta is how two admins on two tabs end up with the
union of what each of them meant.

kind.description: `team` does the work; `client` approves or unblocks it.

title.title: Title
title.description: Who this is, in one line — e.g. 'Finance controller, Atlas'.

responsibilities.title: Responsibilities
responsibilities.description: What they do, and so what you would tag them about when work stalls.

colour.title: Colour
colour.description: Six-digit hex. Omit to take a stable colour from the palette.

PersonKind.title: PersonKind
PersonKind.description: Which side of the work someone is on.

is_agent.title: Is Agent
is_agent.description: Whether this entry is the machine rather than a person. It is assigned work like anybody else and never signs in.

has_account.title: Has Account
has_account.description: Whether they can sign in as themselves right now.

invite_is_pending.title: Invite Is Pending
invite_is_pending.description: Whether an unaccepted, unexpired invitation is outstanding.

PersonRead.title: PersonRead
PersonRead.description:
One directory entry, the same for everybody who asks.

There is deliberately no ``is_me`` here. It used to be a column, because
there used to be one owner; with several people signed in it would have to
mean something different in each response, and a payload whose truth
depends on who fetched it is a payload that cannot be cached, shared or
reasoned about. Whoever is asking already knows who they are — ``GET /me``
told them — so "is this me?" is one comparison on the client and no
ambiguity on the server.

archived.title: Archived
archived.description: Archive them: they leave the pickers and every credential they hold is revoked. Set false to bring them back, password intact.

PersonUpdate.title: PersonUpdate
PersonUpdate.description: Every field optional; omitted fields are left as they are.

task.title: Task
task.description: The card, by reference such as `ATL-41` or by id.

day.title: Day
day.description: Which day to put it on, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

PickRead.title: PickRead
PickRead.description: One card on the caller's plan for a day, with their to-dos under it.

column.title: Column
column.description: The column it sits in now. Null once it has gone to cold storage.

PickedCard.title: PickedCard
PickedCard.description: The card a pick is of: enough to name it without a second request.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `add_section` / `update_section`: into `doc_id`. `new_file`: a new doc under `topic_id`. `add_index_entry`, `update_summary`: keep `doc_id` findable. `add_related`: a `Related:` line in `doc_id` naming `related_path`. `new_topic`: no topic fits — topics are made by people, so file it in the nearest one and say so.

sure.title: Sure
sure.description: False: worth a look, not worth doing blind.

facts.title: Facts
facts.description: Which facts it carries, by position from 0.

path.title: Path
path.description: The doc, `Engineering / MCP / tasks.md`, or the topic a new doc goes under, `Engineering / MCP`.

doc_shape.title: Doc Shape
doc_shape.description: How the doc is written, so the edit matches it. `indexed`: an `## Index` entry `N. Title — blurb` and a matching `## Title` section. `headings`: a `## Title` section. `bullets`: one `- ` line. `plain`: anywhere.

PlannedEdit.title: PlannedEdit
PlannedEdit.description: One edit the plan calls for. Nothing has been written.

url.title: Url
url.description: Where the pull request is — a URL, or a short form such as `#212`. Free text, as the Jira reference is: a URL is the more useful of the two because it can be followed, and the frontend shortens whichever shape it is given.

state.description: How far it got: `raised` while nobody has reviewed it, `approved` once somebody has said yes, `merged` once it is in. Omitted it is `raised`, which is where every pull request starts.

PrRef.title: PrRef
PrRef.description:
One pull request carrying a card's work: where it is, and how far it got.

The state is the whole of what this schema adds over the bare string the
field used to hold, and it is optional on the way in because ``raised`` is

which is why it is the thing holding what an entry may contain: the column

question for the pull request itself, which the reference links to.

is on, so the two travel together in one JSON object — see
:attr:`Task.pr_refs`.

sub_statuses.description: Replaces the whole list of stage labels. The current stage is kept if it still fits, otherwise pulled back to the new last one.

sub_status_index.title: Sub Status Index
sub_status_index.description: Which stage is current, once `sub_statuses` has been applied. Send it when reordering or removing stages has moved the marker — the caller doing the reordering is the only one that knows where it went. Left out, the marker stays where it was.

due_date.title: Due Date
due_date.description: A new date, or null to take the date off the card. Unlike the other fields here, null means clear rather than leave alone.

column_due_dates.title: Column Due Dates
column_due_dates.description: Replaces every per-column date the card has: send the whole set, an empty list to take them all off, or leave it out to leave them alone. A list rather than a patch per column because that is how the dates are read — as one schedule across the board.

template_id.title: Template Id
template_id.description: A different template, or null to take the card out of one entirely. Like `due_date`, null here means clear rather than leave alone. Refused if the card's current column is one the new template does not allow — move it first. The card's current `sub_statuses` are left as they are; a new template's stages are not retroactively applied, only picked up the next time the card lands somewhere new.

goal_id.title: Goal Id
goal_id.description: A different goal, or null to unlink the card from the one it is on. Like `due_date`, null here means clear rather than leave alone. Refused on a sub-task: a sub-task belongs to its card, and its card is what belongs to a goal.

jira_ref.title: Jira Ref
jira_ref.description: A different Jira issue, or null to take the reference off. Like `due_date`, null here means clear rather than leave alone.

pr_refs.title: Pr Refs
pr_refs.description: The whole list of pull requests this card is carried by, replacing whatever it had: this is how one is added, how one is removed, and how one is moved from `raised` to `approved` to `merged`. An empty list takes them all off, and leaving the field out leaves them alone — which is why null is not how they are cleared here.

TaskUpdate.title: TaskUpdate
TaskUpdate.description:
Every field optional; omitted fields are left as they are.

Status is not here: it moves through ``POST /tasks/{ref}/status``, which is
the only path that can demand a reason and record one.

description.title: Description
description.description: What kind of card this is. Optional — a template is a word on a card, and "Hotfix" already explains itself.

stages.title: Stages
stages.description: One entry per column this template's cards may sit in, naming the sub-stages a card passes through in each before it may leave. Empty means unrestricted — a template may gain its rule later.

stages.title: Stages
stages.description: In the board's own left-to-right order.

allowed_column_ids.title: Allowed Column Ids
allowed_column_ids.description: The stages' column ids, in the same order — a convenience for a client that only needs to know where a card may go, not what sub-stages it passes through there. **Empty means unrestricted**: this template has no stages yet, so its cards go anywhere on the board.

task_count.title: Task Count
task_count.description: How many cards were created from this template.

TemplateUpdate.title: TemplateUpdate
TemplateUpdate.description:
Every field optional; omitted fields are left as they are.

``stages`` is the exception to "partial": sending it replaces the whole
set. A template's rule is read as one thing — the stages together are the
policy — so it is edited and saved as one thing rather than column by
column.

picks.title: Picks
picks.description: In the order the cards were picked.

open_count.title: Open Count
open_count.description: To-dos still open on the day.

TodayPlan.title: TodayPlan
TodayPlan.description: The caller's plan for one day on one project.

text.title: Text
text.description: What to do, as written — `@Aditi K` and `>brief.pdf` tags included.

state.description: `open`, `done`, `moved` (handed on at wrap-up — `moved_to` says where) or `not_done` (left behind at wrap-up).

moved_to.title: Moved To
moved_to.description: The day it was handed on to, when it was.

carried_from.title: Carried From
carried_from.description: The day it was handed on from, when it arrived by wrap-up.

source_kind.title: Source Kind
source_kind.description: What on the card it stands for, when it came from the card: a stage, a sub-task or a tick box. Ticking it ticks that too, and the other way about. Null for a to-do somebody wrote.

TodoRead.title: TodoRead
TodoRead.description: One thing to do about a card, on one day.

state.title: State
state.description: Tick it (`done`), untick it (`open`) or give up on it (`not_done`). `moved` is what wrap-up sets, never this.

name.title: Name
name.description: What this token is for, e.g. 'board-tidy agent'.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.description: Grant the narrowest set that still lets the client do its job.

expires_in_days.title: Expires In Days
expires_in_days.description: Omit for a token that never expires.

person_id.title: Person Id
person_id.description: Whose authority this token carries — whoever minted it. Null only for tokens minted before accounts existed, and for one minted from the bootstrap session.

token.title: Token
token.description: Copy this now — it is never shown again.

TokenIssued.title: TokenIssued
TokenIssued.description: A freshly minted token, including the only copy of its plaintext.

person_id.title: Person Id
person_id.description: Whose authority this token carries — whoever minted it. Null only for tokens minted before accounts existed, and for one minted from the bootstrap session.

parent_id.title: Parent Id
parent_id.description: The branch to create this under. Omit for the top level.

kind.description: `branch` holds other nodes; `secret` holds one credential.

sensitivity.description: How far this may travel. Omit to inherit the parent branch's, or the tree's default at the top level.

parent_id.title: Parent Id
parent_id.description: The branch to move under, within the same tree. `null` moves the node to the top level; this field is always the new parent, never 'leave it where it is'.

VaultNodeMove.title: VaultNodeMove
VaultNodeMove.description: Where a node should end up.

sensitivity.description: How far this may travel. A role not cleared this high is not shown it.

secret.description: Present on a `secret` node. Never includes the value.

children.title: Children
children.description: The subtree beneath this node, in position order.

sensitivity.description: Reclassify it. Raising a branch's level hides everything under it from anybody not cleared that far.

VaultNodeUpdate.title: VaultNodeUpdate
VaultNodeUpdate.description:
Every field optional; omitted fields are left as they are.

``kind`` is deliberately absent. Turning a secret into a branch would have
to decide what happens to the credential underneath it, and "silently
discard it" is not an answer worth shipping — delete the node instead.

default_sensitivity.description: What nodes added to this tree are classified as unless the caller says. A tree is how a vault is already divided, so this is where "everything in Certificates is restricted" is said once.
What nodes added here are classified as unless the caller says.

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.description: Top-level nodes, each nesting its own.

VaultTreeDetail.title: VaultTreeDetail
VaultTreeDetail.description: A tree with everything in it — and not one secret value.

default_sensitivity.description: What nodes added here are classified as unless the caller says.

VaultTreeUpdate.title: VaultTreeUpdate
VaultTreeUpdate.description: Every field optional; omitted fields are left as they are.

to_day.title: To Day
to_day.description: Where the moved to-dos go. Must be after `day`.

move.title: Move
move.description: The open to-dos to hand on. Every other open to-do on the day stays behind as `not_done`.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA zone that says what today is, e.g. `Asia/Kolkata`. Defaults to UTC. A day from today on is brought in step with its cards before it is closed; a day gone by is closed on the plan it had.
